newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Ministers reject military action on Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: Ministers reject military action on Zaire crisis.

text.p: African foreign ministers have rejected military involvement to end the violence engulfing the Great Lakes region of Central Africa.

The ministers met in Pretoria for two days of crisis talks on the violence in eastern Zaire, where the army has begun a battle to regain rebel-held territory, and after reports of new massacres in Burundi and Rwanda.

"The meeting...called upon all countries, organisations and foreign nationals to refrain from military involvement in the conflict, which could lead to a further escalation of hostilities," the ministers said in a statement released on Tuesday night.

The foreign ministers of Cameroon, Congo, South Africa, Tanzania and Zimbabwe, meeting under the chairmanship of Kenyan Foreign Minister Stephen Musyoka, had decided to visit Zaire as soon as possible for talks with the Kinshasa government.
"It was also decided that the visit should be followed by similar visits to Burundi, Rwanda and Uganda in search of a lasting solution to the crisis in the Great Lakes region," the statement said.
A regional summit on the troubled Great Lakes region in December charged the group of ministers, led by Kenya, to take charge of efforts to end the crisis.
Rebels seized Zaire's eastern borderlands late last year, sparking an exodus of more than a million ethnic Hutu refugees from the camps they had lived in since fleeing Rwanda in 1994.
The rebellion sent giant Zaire, already unstable, deeper into chaos.
Violence has flared in several areas of Rwanda since the return of many of the Hutu refugees to their homeland, which is ruled by a government dominated by ethnic Tutsis.
There have also been recent reports of massacres in Burundi, where Tutsi strongman Pierre Buyoya was installed by the army as military ruler after a coup last July.
